changelog: Insert a single 'fallback' preference that, as a last resort, orders cuts to favor positions after essential post‑nominal modifiers rather than between a noun/numeral head and its modifier — addresses the primary finding that heads were being split from immediately following essential modifiers.

Insert a single narrow surface check that binds a noun or numeral to an immediately following essential post‑nominal modifier, addressing the primary finding that heads were being split from their modifiers.
Replace E1 with labeled example en_us_375 to teach the model about keeping a numeral with its measurement/unit parenthetical (primary finding: protect noun/numeral + immediate essential modifier).

Replace E2 with labeled example en_us_101 to show a noun/numeral followed immediately by a restrictive clause and a measurement parenthetical (reinforces the need not to split head from essential post‑nominal modifier).
Replace E3 with labeled example en_us_1253 to illustrate a noun followed by an essential prepositional complement (protect NP + immediate PP).
Replace E4 with labeled example en_us_1157 to provide a measurement post‑nominal modifier case (+30°C) so the judge learns to keep measurements attached.

delete C3 — remove a redundant predicate–argument protection that restates C2 so the prompt is leaner and avoids dividing the judge's attention; chosen under the 'prune' constraint because C3 overlaps C2 (which must be kept per measured lessons) and carries no measured gain.
